findings.claim: retarget_file_tags resolves a tag by Python-folded key to the oldest variant, ignoring an exact-name row on the destination, and treats non-ASCII case variants as one tag while tag editing and the tag filter treat them as two.
findings.impact: A file tagged `übung` that could be found by its tag on the source drive can stop being found after a move. The move answers 200 and the tag chip reads `Übung`, but choosing either spelling on the destination does not list the file, even when that drive also has a row named exactly `übung`. A note's frontmatter keeps `übung`, so the next projection moves it to a separate `übung` row and the tag counts shift again.
findings.evidence: `backend/app/services/tagops.py:52-53` keeps the lowest-id row for each `name.lower()`, and `tagops.py:59` looks up only that key, so an exact-name row with a higher id is never chosen. `backend/app/routers/files.py:159-168` (`replace_file_tags`) compares SQL `lower(Tag.name)`, which folds ASCII only, so `Übung` and `übung` can coexist on one drive through normal tagging when `Übung` is created first. `backend/app/routers/drives.py:716` filters with `func.lower(Tag.name) == name.lower()`, so both spellings select only the `übung` row, and a file linked to `Übung` is never listed. `docs/developer-guide/known-issues.md:204` records that a non-ASCII capital lists nothing when chosen. `backend/tests/test_move_tags_follow_drive.py` `test_a_non_ascii_case_variant_is_reused_without_renaming` asserts the variant merge, and `test_a_destination_holding_two_variants_resolves_to_the_older_row` covers only a destination with no exact-name row. The code replaced in this commit compared SQL `lower(Tag.name)` with the folded key, so it found a lowercase exact-name row.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only review; derived from the code). Steps: on drive B, tag file 1 `Übung`, then tag file 2 `übung`, which leaves two rows. On drive A, tag file 3 `übung` and move it to B. Expected from the code: B lists `Übung` 2 and `übung` 1, and `GET /api/drives/B/files?tag=übung` returns file 2 but not file 3. A mutant that looks up the exact name first would pass every current test.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariants are declared. Normal tagging reaches this and the result is silently wrong, but it needs non-ASCII cased names that differ between drives.

findings.proposed_fix: Look up the exact name on the destination first and fall back to the folded key only when there is no exact row, and add a test with both variants on the destination. Whether a non-ASCII variant should merge at all is a decision for a person, because the filter and `replace_file_tags` still treat variants as different tags.

findings.claim: Editing the tags of a file that holds a non-ASCII capital tag fails on `uq_tags_drive_name`, because `replace_file_tags` still has the folding mismatch this commit removed from the move path.
findings.impact: After a successful move onto a reused `Übung` row, adding or removing another tag on that file answers 500 and nothing changes. For a note, the frontmatter has already been rewritten when the projection fails, so `File.tags` and the frontmatter disagree. The same mismatch makes a knowledge scanner tag post fail for that file. The failure also occurs without a move, for any file holding such a tag.
findings.evidence: `backend/app/routers/files.py:162` compares SQL `lower(Tag.name)` with Python `tag_name.lower()`. For `Übung` the two differ, so the lookup misses and `files.py:168` builds a second `Tag` with the same drive and name. `backend/app/models.py:47` rejects it at the flush in `cleanup_orphan_tags`. `files.py:817-819` has no handler for that error. `files.py:796-803` answers 500 `Tag projection failed` after the content write. `backend/app/routers/internal.py:165-166` calls the same helper. `merge_file_tags` at `files.py:198-206` has the same lookup and flush. The validator at `backend/app/schemas.py:129` accepts the name, and no `create_function` or ICU registration exists in `backend/app`. `docs/developer-guide/known-issues.md:204` records only the listing symptom. The new tests in `TestNonAsciiTagNames` stop at the tag list after the move and never edit tags afterwards.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only review; derived from the code). Steps: tag a non-Markdown file `Übung`, then send `PUT /api/files/{id}/tags` with `Übung` and a second valid tag. Expected from the code: an unhandled IntegrityError and a 500, with the file's tags unchanged.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariants are declared. The failure is loud and predates this change, and whether to fix it here is a decision for a person.

findings.proposed_fix: Match names in `replace_file_tags` and `merge_file_tags` with the same rule as the move path, through one shared helper, and add a test that edits tags on a file holding a non-ASCII capital tag.

findings.claim: A file still linked to another drive's tag row by the old code strands that row when its tags are edited or it is purged, because those paths sweep only `file.drive`.
findings.impact: On a database that had cross-drive moves before this fix, editing such a file's tags or purging it leaves a tag on the old drive listed with count 0. The row stays until something else sweeps that drive. The sweep added in this commit covers only the next cross-drive move, and the known-issues text no longer describes the purge case.
findings.evidence: `backend/app/services/fileops.py:697-701` (`physical_delete`) and `backend/app/routers/files.py:817-818` sweep the file's current drive only. `backend/app/routers/drives.py:814-819` keeps rows with no linked file in the listing. `tagops.py:45-46` returns early for a same-drive move, so that path repairs nothing. `tagops.py:54` and `tagops.py:61-62` are the only multi-drive sweep. `TestMoveSweepsEveryDriveTheTagsCameFrom` exercises only a cross-drive move.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only review; derived from the code). Steps: link a file on drive B to a `Tag` on drive A, as the old code left it, and make that file the row's only user. Trash and purge the file, or `PUT` its tags with a different list. Expected from the code: A's tag list still has the row, with count 0.

bucket_proposal.reason: The stale links come from the defect this change fixes, and the author chose not to migrate them. The result is a cosmetic count-0 row on one drive.

findings.proposed_fix: A one-time startup repair of links whose `Tag.drive` differs from `File.drive` would remove this whole class. Sweeping the old rows' drives in the tag-edit and purge paths is the narrower option.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change, so bucket A is unavailable and no touch-point list can be exceeded.

R1 finding on non-ASCII capitals: resolved for the failure. `tagops.py:51-53` and `tagops.py:59` match in Python, so an identical name always finds its row and no duplicate is built. `Tag(...)` is reached only when no destination row has that key, so `uq_tags_drive_name` cannot fire on a tag name in this function. F1 is the side effect of this choice.

R1 finding on the pending-delete row: resolved. `db.flush()` at `tagops.py:49` runs before the destination query, so the row deleted by `resolve_db_path_conflict` (`fileops.py:191-194`) is gone from the query result, and a new row is created. `left_drives - {dst_drive}` at `tagops.py:61` also keeps the sweep off the destination.

R1 finding on legacy links: partly resolved. A cross-drive move now sweeps the drives of the rows the file held (`tagops.py:54`, `tagops.py:61-62`). No migration was added, and known-issues.md records that decision. F3 covers the paths that remain.

`file.drive` is assigned only at `fileops.py:497`, and a grep of `backend/app` for `SET drive` and `UPDATE tags` found nothing. Both move endpoints go through `move_file`, and the single endpoint checks destination access at `files.py:1433`.
`Tag.drive` is non-nullable (`models.py:37`), so `sorted(left_drives - {dst_drive})` cannot meet None, and `cleanup_orphan_tags(db, None)`, the sweep of every drive, is unreachable from this path.

Scope: known-issues.md gains entries unrelated to tag moves. Those for `readonly`, the note frontmatter and the stale sidebar match the R-5 record in decisions.md. The `/similar/{file_id}` entry does not appear in that record. These are documentation only, and I raise no finding.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A move merges non-ASCII case variants, while `replace_file_tags`, `merge_file_tags` and the tag filter keep them distinct. The tests pin this merge under an `UNSPEC` comment, so a person should confirm it.

When a legacy link is present, the move sweeps orphan rows on a third drive that is neither source nor destination, and that drive may be locked for the requester. Only rows with no linked file are deleted and nothing is returned, so no data is exposed, but the transaction writes outside the two drives named in the request.
The `files.moved` event names only the source and destination drives (`files.py:1438`, `files.py:422`), so an open tab on a swept third drive is not told its tag list changed.

A `.md` file moved onto a row with a different ASCII spelling keeps its frontmatter spelling, and a later projection renames the destination row for every file on that drive (`files.py:169-172`). This is unchanged from r1.
regression_risks: `_move_thumbnail` at `fileops.py:491` is still not reversed by the except block at `fileops.py:508-517`. This commit removes the tag-name trigger, so the remaining triggers are other database errors, such as a concurrent writer.

Each cross-drive move now loads every tag row of the destination drive, once per file in a batch. This is linear in tags times files, and only tag columns are read, so it is not a concern at personal-library size.
R-5 in decisions.md was recorded at 295ba729f, before this commit changed tag matching and sweeping. Non-ASCII names and legacy links have not been walked in the app.
test_coverage: Expected to be killed, by reading: removing `db.flush()` at `tagops.py:49` (trashed-record test), replacing the Python map with an exact-name lookup (case-variant tests), `setdefault` becoming assignment or dropping `.order_by(Tag.id)` (two-variants test, given the index order), and sweeping only `src_drive` (stale-links test).

Expected to survive, by reading: removing `{src_drive} |` at `tagops.py:54`. Every seeded file with tags on the source already contributes that drive, and the stale-links test has no orphan on the drive it leaves. It would change only the sweep of unrelated orphans.
Expected to survive, by reading: removing `- {dst_drive}` at `tagops.py:61`. The earlier flush in `cleanup_orphan_tags` has already linked the reused row, so no test observes the difference.
Expected to survive, by reading: an exact-name-first lookup. No test seeds a destination holding both an exact-name row and an older variant (F1).

Not covered: editing tags after a move onto a non-ASCII capital row (F2), filtering by tag after such a move (F1), purging or re-tagging a file with a legacy link (F3), and a failed move of a video with a thumbnail.

The fixture restores `config.DRIVES_CONFIG` and `_drives_cache` in its teardown, and the third-drive test writes only inside `tmp_path`, so that test should not leak drives. I read the restore of `DRIVES_CONFIG` directly and inferred the rest from the saved `orig` values, because I stopped reading at line 132.

SQLite's ASCII-only `lower()` rests on the absence of a `create_function` registration in `backend/app` and on the known-issues note; the SQLite build in the image was not inspected.
The frontend sending the full tag list on an edit, which is the UI route into F2. I relied on the rule in design-decisions.md that saves go through `saveFileTags` and did not read that code.
How often the knowledge scanner re-projects a moved note, and how it reacts to a failed tag post beyond the status check in `addons/knowledge/app/internal_client.py:240`.
`_write_md_tags` before line 785 of `backend/app/routers/files.py`, and the remaining reads of tag data in addons beyond the grep results and the `tag_knn.py` lookup.
The `/similar/{file_id}` known-issues claim: I confirmed the route exists at `addons/intelligence/app/routers/similar.py:17` but did not read its gating.

perspectives.name: scope
perspectives.notes: Code changes are limited to `tagops.py` and its test. `fileops.py` changes only by the single call inside the try block. The rest of the commit is known-issues text, and no other path changes a file's drive.

perspectives.name: submodules
perspectives.notes: No gitlink changes. Addons read `tags` and `file_tags` by name or drive with no stored tag ids in the grep results, so replacing a file's Tag rows breaks no reference found. `addons/intelligence/app/workers/tag_knn.py:220-224` drops rows labelled for another drive, so legacy links stay ignored until they are moved, and correct links reduce that drift.

perspectives.name: persistence
perspectives.notes: All retarget writes are inside the try block of `move_file` and roll back together. New rows cannot collide, the destination is not swept, and the early flush makes pending deletes visible before the lookup. F1 and F3 are the remaining wrong-state cases, and F2 is the sibling path that still has the old mismatch.

perspectives.name: concurrency
perspectives.notes: Each request has its own session, and a batch commits per file with a rollback on failure, so each file's lookup sees committed rows. The destination SELECT can race another request's sweep of the same orphan row or an insert of the same new name. Both end in a constraint error and a reversed 500, not silent damage, and a single user is unlikely to hit it. No finding is raised.

trajectory: The record holds one code fix round after the original change, because 714a2ae57 only records the review. That round removed one thing: the per-name SQL lookup and its `if key in retargeted: continue` branch became a single Python map. It added two things of different kinds: an ordering prediction (`db.flush()` must run before the lookup so pending deletes are gone) and a new state (`left_drives`, the set of drives to sweep). Neither repeats something the first round added, so one round shows no repeated patching of the same kind. The matching rule is the place to watch: it changed in this round and still differs from `replace_file_tags`, `merge_file_tags` and the tag filter, which is the source of F1 and F2. Another round that adjusts matching only in the move path would mean the design is being patched.
